steps.tx: Diabetic nephropathy glomerulosclerosis thickens basement membranes, expands mesangium, and drops podocytes under hyperglycaemia and hyperfiltration until albuminuria and declining filtration march through stages. That metabolic scarring is **diabetic nephropathy (diabetic kidney disease)**. This point is tested repeatedly because it changes everyday bedside decisions.
steps.say: Albuminuria then falling filtration over diabetic years is diabetic nephropathy until red flags object.

steps.tx: Kimmelstiel-Wilson nodules laminate mesangial matrix into PAS positive balls beside capsular drops and fibrin caps, pathognomonic accents among diabetic glomerular lesions. Those nodules are the **Kimmelstiel-Wilson nodules of diabetes**. Examiners return to it because it separates careful clinicians from guesswork. Bedside recognition of this pattern saves time, blood, and unnecessary investigation.
steps.say: Laminated mesangial balls are Kimmelstiel-Wilson nodules, diabetes written in glomerular matrix.

steps.tx: Albuminuria categories A1 to A3 and eGFR stages jointly map diabetic kidney disease while retinopathy supports attribution in type one diabetes more reliably than type two. That grid is **diabetic kidney disease albuminuria and eGFR staging**. Students should anchor this fact before moving to rarer causes and exceptions.
steps.say: Stage diabetic kidneys by albumin and filtration together; either alone understates risk.

steps.tx: Red flags against pure diabetic nephropathy include haematuria with casts, rapid progression, nephrotic syndrome early in type one disease, absent retinopathy discordance, and systemic autoimmune signs. Those demand biopsy: **atypical diabetic kidney presentation, biopsy triggers**. In practice this distinction decides the next test, treatment, or referral made.
steps.say: Bloody casts or five year type one nephrotic syndrome are not diabetic nephropathy until biopsy agrees.

vis.caption: Amyloid nephropathy, a nodular glomerular mimic diabetic biopsy must exclude.

steps.tx: Hyperfiltration injures early diabetic kidneys through glomerular hypertension that RAAS blockade and SGLT2 inhibition relieve haemodynamically while glucose and pressure control slow the metabolic fire. That dual protection is **haemodynamic therapy in diabetic kidney disease**. That is why this detail earns its place in every examination and ward round.
steps.say: RAAS and SGLT2 drugs lower glomerular pressure mechanically; glucose control cools the cause upstream.

nodes.label: RAAS and SGLT2 lower intraglomerular pressure

steps.tx: Armanni-Ebstein glycogen vacuoles stuff proximal tubule cells in severe hyperglycaemia and ketoacidosis historically, a biopsy curiosity beside hyaline arteriolosclerosis shared with hypertension. That tubular signature is the **Armanni-Ebstein change of uncontrolled diabetes**. Remembering it prevents the commonest errors made with this presentation entirely.
steps.say: Glycogen vacuolated tubules are Armanni-Ebstein change, uncontrolled diabetes leaving tubular fingerprints.

steps.tx: Cardiovascular death outruns kidney failure in diabetic kidney disease, so statins, smoking cessation, pressure, and modern glucose agents with cardiac benefit share prescriptions equally. That priority is **cardiovascular protection in diabetic kidney disease**. The clinical payoff comes from applying it early, before complications accumulate further.
steps.say: Most diabetic kidney patients die cardiovascularly first; protect hearts with the same prescription pad.

steps.tx: Non albuminuric diabetic kidney disease declines filtration behind vascular and tubulointerstitial injury despite clean urine, defeating albumin only screening in older type two patients. That phenotype is **non-albuminuric diabetic kidney disease**. This point is tested repeatedly because it changes everyday bedside decisions.
steps.say: Falling filtration with bland albumin still counts in diabetes; screen eGFR beside urine ratios.
